questions.stem: What is another term used for fish farming according to the lecture note?
questions.explanation: The lecture note explicitly defines fish farming as pisciculture.

questions.stem: Fish farming involves the commercial breeding of fishes primarily for what purpose?
questions.explanation: The note states fish farming involves breeding fishes most known for food.

questions.stem: Where can the commercial breeding of fish take place according to the text?
questions.explanation: The text mentions breeding occurs either in the natural environment or in an artificial enclosure such as ponds.

questions.stem: In which part of Nigeria is fish farming noted to be popular?

options.C: Southern part and some areas in the North

questions.explanation: The note states fish farming is popular in the Southern part of Nigeria and some areas in the North.

questions.stem: What is defined as the way or means in which water enters a pond?
questions.explanation: An inlet is described as a way or means in which water enters the ponds.

questions.stem: What is defined as the means in which water goes out of a pond?
questions.explanation: An outlet is described as a means in which water goes out.

questions.stem: What is the term for breeding only one species of fish?
questions.explanation: The breeding of one species of fish is called monoculture.

questions.stem: What is the term for breeding two or more species of fishes?
questions.explanation: The breeding of two or more species is called poly-culture.

questions.stem: Which of the following are the two most common species of fish reared in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The text lists Tilapia and Catfish as the two most common species reared in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Why is fish farming considered a lucrative business in Nigeria's Agro-business sector?
questions.explanation: The note states it is lucrative due to its rich source of protein.

questions.stem: According to the note, which nutrient is high in fish and only found in fishes?
questions.explanation: The lecture note specifically mentions 'Omega-2, which can only be found in fishes'.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT listed as a type of fresh water in the note?
questions.explanation: Sea is categorized under Marine Water/Salt Water, not Fresh water.

questions.stem: Which of the following is categorized as Marine Water/Salt Water?
questions.explanation: The note lists Ocean under Marine Water/Salt Water.

questions.stem: What are the two main types of fish based on body structure mentioned in the text?
questions.explanation: The text classifies the two types of fish as Bony and Cartilaginous.

questions.stem: What is the defining characteristic of Bony fishes?

options.D: They are only found in the South

questions.explanation: Bony fishes are defined as those that have bone-supporting structures.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a Bony fish?
questions.explanation: The note lists Tilapia and Mackerel as examples of Bony fishes.

questions.stem: What is the defining characteristic of Cartilaginous fishes?

options.B: They have cartilage as their body-supporting structure
options.D: They are exclusively used for poly-culture

questions.explanation: Cartilaginous fishes are defined as those that have cartilage as their body-supporting structure.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a Cartilaginous fish?
questions.explanation: The note lists shark and dogfish as examples of cartilaginous fishes.

questions.stem: Before 1945, what was the nature of the fishing industry in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The text states the industry before the Second World War (1945) was largely artisanal.

questions.stem: In 1941, the colonial government established what to carry out the transfer of fishes to Cameroon?

options.B: Colonial development of commerce and industry

questions.explanation: The note says the colonial government established this body in 1941 for fish transfer to Cameroon.

questions.stem: Which event marked the inception of fish culture in Nigeria?

options.C: Construction of the Panyal Fish Farm in 1944

questions.explanation: The text states the 1944 construction marked the inception of fish culture in Nigeria.

questions.stem: The Panyal Fish Farm was specifically constructed for the production of which fish?
questions.explanation: The text refers to the 'Panyal Fish Farm for Tilapia Production'.

questions.stem: In what year were government pilot schemes set up to raise local fish species in places like Ibadan and Lagos?
questions.explanation: The note states government pilot schemes were set up in 1950.

questions.stem: Which location was NOT mentioned as a site for the 1950 government pilot schemes?
questions.explanation: The sites mentioned for 1950 are Ibadan, Ikoyi, Lagos, and Okigwe.

questions.stem: What was the name of the nationwide campaign launched in 1964?
questions.explanation: The text identifies the 1964 campaign as 'Grow Your Own Fish'.

questions.stem: What was the result of the 1964 nationwide campaign?

options.B: A remarkable and tremendous increase in the number of fish farm

questions.explanation: The note states a remarkable increase was noticed after the 1964 campaign.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a listed benefit of fish farming in Nigeria regarding the national economy?

options.B: It serves as a source of foreign exchange

questions.explanation: The text lists serving as a source of foreign exchange as a benefit.

questions.stem: How does fish farming contribute to the economic growth of the country?

options.A: By providing steady income and employment opportunities
options.B: By reducing the cost of meat

questions.explanation: The note states it contributes by providing steady income and employment opportunities.

questions.stem: Which benefit refers to the reliability of food supply mentioned in the text?
questions.explanation: Food security is explicitly listed as a benefit of fish farming.

questions.stem: Fish farming helps reduce the importation of what commodity?
questions.explanation: The note mentions it 'reduce importation of fish' as a benefit.

questions.stem: According to the note, what does fish farming reduce the potency of?
questions.explanation: The text states it 'reduces the potency of wild livestock'.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a concept under 'Environmental sustainability' in the lecture note?
questions.explanation: Efficiency resources use is listed under Environmental sustainability.

questions.stem: Environmental protection is categorized under which heading in the note?
questions.explanation: Environmental protection is listed under the Environmental sustainability heading.

questions.stem: According to the history section, where were people mostly fishing before 1945?
questions.explanation: The text states people were fishing mostly in the lagoon, riverine and swampy areas before 1945.

questions.stem: What does NFDC stand for in the context of the 1971 reference?
questions.explanation: The text explicitly defines NFDC as Nigeria Fishery Development Commission.

questions.stem: Which of the following is specifically listed as a type of Fresh water?
questions.explanation: Streams is listed under the category of Fresh waters.

questions.stem: According to the note, where is Tilapia and Catfish protein beneficial and of value?
questions.explanation: The note states it is a rich source of protein which is beneficial and of value to our daily life.

questions.stem: Which year is associated with the first attempt by the colonial government to develop fishes?
questions.explanation: The text states that in 1941 the colonial government made the first attempt to develop fishes.

questions.stem: Which type of fish has bone-supporting structures?
questions.explanation: The note defines Bony fishes as those that have bone-supporting structures.

questions.stem: Which of the following practices supports sustainable fish farming?
questions.explanation: Proper waste management helps protect the environment and ensures sustainable fish farming.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes aquaculture in relation to fish farming?

options.A: The harvesting of wild fish only
options.B: The scientific study of fish behavior
options.C: The controlled cultivation of aquatic organisms
options.D: Fishing carried out in oceans only

questions.explanation: Aquaculture broadly refers to the controlled cultivation of aquatic organisms, including fish farming.

questions.stem: Which factor is most important for successful fish farming?
questions.explanation: Good water quality is essential for fish survival, growth, and overall productivity in fish farming.

questions.stem: Which feeding practice helps promote faster growth in cultured fish?
questions.explanation: Balanced nutrition given at regular intervals promotes healthy and faster fish growth.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common challenge faced in fish farming?
questions.explanation: Disease outbreaks are a major challenge in fish farming and can reduce productivity.

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of aeration in fish ponds?

options.C: To increase oxygen level in water

questions.explanation: Aeration helps increase dissolved oxygen, which is vital for fish respiration.

questions.stem: Which of the following farming systems involves raising fish in artificial ponds?
questions.explanation: Pond culture is a fish farming system where fish are raised in artificial ponds.

questions.stem: Why is record keeping important in fish farming?

options.B: To monitor growth, feeding, and profit

questions.explanation: Record keeping helps farmers track performance, costs, and productivity.

questions.stem: Which of the following predators can negatively affect fish ponds?
questions.explanation: Predators such as birds and snakes can feed on fish and reduce stock.

questions.stem: Which water condition is most suitable for most freshwater fish species?
questions.explanation: Freshwater fish thrive best in clean water with sufficient oxygen.

questions.stem: According to the document, what is another name for Fish Farming?
questions.explanation: The text explicitly states: 'Fish farming, also called aquaculture...'

questions.stem: What is the term used for a young fish in the provided material?
questions.explanation: In the objective questions, 'Fingerling' is identified as the term for a young fish.

questions.stem: Which of these is defined as a facility where fish eggs are hatched?
questions.explanation: The document identifies the hatchery as the place where fish eggs are hatched.

questions.stem: Which fish farming system is specifically mentioned as suitable for areas with limited space?
questions.explanation: The document states tank culture is suitable where there is limited space.

questions.stem: What is the primary effect of pond fertilization according to the text?
questions.explanation: The notes indicate that pond fertilization helps to increase natural food for the fish.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of good water quality mentioned in the notes?
questions.explanation: Good water quality promotes healthy growth, while poor quality is what causes mortality.

questions.stem: According to the document, what happens if fish are overfed?
questions.explanation: The document states that overfeeding fish can lead to water pollution.

questions.stem: In the context of fish farming, what does 'Mortality' mean?
questions.explanation: The objective section defines mortality as death.

questions.stem: Which factor would most likely increase fish mortality in a pond?
questions.explanation: Overcrowding and poor water quality reduce oxygen levels and increase stress and disease, leading to mortality.

questions.stem: Why is stocking density important in fish farming?

options.B: It affects fish growth and survival

questions.explanation: Too many fish per pond reduces oxygen and increases competition, affecting survival and growth.

questions.stem: A farmer notices slow fish growth despite regular feeding. Which factor should be checked first?
questions.explanation: Poor water quality affects metabolism and growth even if feeding is adequate.

questions.stem: Which of the following best explains why fish farming reduces overfishing?

options.A: It replaces wild fish supply with farmed fish

questions.explanation: Farmed fish reduce pressure on wild fish populations.

questions.stem: What is the likely result of harvesting fish before they reach market size?
questions.explanation: Smaller fish sell for lower prices, reducing profitability.

questions.stem: Which fish farming system would be most appropriate in a river?
questions.explanation: Cage culture is practiced in natural flowing water bodies like rivers.

questions.stem: Why should fingerlings be healthy and active before stocking?

options.B: To ensure better survival and growth

questions.explanation: Healthy fingerlings have higher survival rates and better growth performance.

questions.stem: Which practice improves environmental sustainability in fish farming?

options.B: Efficient resource use and waste management

questions.explanation: Sustainable practices protect the environment and ensure long-term productivity.

questions.stem: A farmer wants to start fish farming in a small urban area. Which system is most suitable?
questions.explanation: Tank culture is suitable for areas with limited space.

questions.stem: Which stage directly follows stocking in fish production?
questions.explanation: After stocking, fish are fed and managed until they reach market size.

questions.stem: What is the relationship between feed cost and profitability?

options.A: Higher feed cost always increases profit
options.B: Feed cost has no impact on profit
options.C: Feed cost is a major factor affecting profit
options.D: Feed cost only affects pond color

questions.explanation: Feed is a major operational cost and directly affects net profit.

questions.stem: Which management practice helps prevent disease outbreak?
questions.explanation: Good hygiene and monitoring reduce disease spread.

questions.stem: Fish require dissolved oxygen primarily for what purpose?
questions.explanation: Fish use dissolved oxygen for respiration to survive.

questions.stem: Which factor best determines when fish should be harvested?
questions.explanation: Fish are harvested when they reach market size and demand is favorable.

questions.stem: If a pond lacks proper drainage, what is the likely consequence?
questions.explanation: Proper drainage is essential for water control and harvesting.

questions.stem: Which of the following is both an economic and nutritional benefit of fish farming?
questions.explanation: Fish farming provides protein-rich food and generates income.

questions.stem: If feed cost increases while the selling price of fish remains the same, what is the most likely outcome?
questions.explanation: When production cost increases without an increase in selling price, profit margin decreases.

questions.stem: Which sequence correctly represents the basic stages of fish production?
questions.explanation: Fish are first stocked, then fed and managed, and finally harvested at market size.

questions.stem: Which factor is MOST critical to monitor daily in a fish pond?
questions.explanation: Water quality directly affects oxygen levels, fish health, and survival.

questions.stem: If a farmer ignores water testing for a long period, what is the most likely chain reaction?

options.B: Poor water quality → Disease outbreak → Mortality

questions.explanation: Unchecked poor water conditions promote disease and lead to fish death.

questions.stem: Which farming system offers the greatest control over environmental conditions?
questions.explanation: Tank culture allows better control of feeding, water quality, and stocking density.

questions.stem: What is the economic importance of reducing fish mortality?

options.B: It reduces total harvest and income
options.C: It increases harvest quantity and profitability

questions.explanation: Lower mortality means more fish survive to market size, increasing total yield and profit.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST indicator of good fish health?

options.B: Active swimming and regular feeding response

questions.explanation: Healthy fish are active and respond well during feeding.

questions.stem: If a farmer practices polyculture, what is the main advantage?
questions.explanation: Different species can occupy different ecological niches, maximizing resource use.

questions.stem: Which of the following decisions would MOST likely increase profitability?
questions.explanation: Efficient feeding reduces waste and improves growth, increasing profit.

questions.stem: Why is proper pond drainage important during harvesting?

options.B: To simplify fish collection and reduce stress

questions.explanation: Controlled drainage makes harvesting easier and minimizes fish injury or loss.
